messages:
Ava (CEO): Thanks everyone — quick follow-up from the all-hands Q&A about why we win/lose and the asks that bubbled up. I wanted to capture hypotheses and clear next owners so we actually close the loop.

Sam (Head of Product): High level recap: recurring asks were around predictable latency tiers, clearer quantization guidance, and a simpler migration path from hosted -> dedicated. Also a lot of customers asked for sample SLO configs.

Ravi (Sales): Confirming — two mid-market losses last quarter mentioned price predictability + lack of private deployment checklist. Both brought up wanting a conservative throughput estimate.

Elena (Customer Success): On the wins side, customers called out our rollout fallback (canary -> auto-failover) as a differentiator. They love the console traces that show per-request cost.

Marta (Eng Manager): Quick note: we have an internal draft on quantization profiles but it's not public. We can turn it into a short "how-to" by end of month. Assigning to me to drive.

Sam (Head of Product): Action item: create 1-pager SLO templates (latency/availability/cost) for self-serve customers. Jordan can you partner on examples for PLG?

Jordan (Growth): Yep — I'll assemble 3 real usage templates (chat, embeddings, batch-rerank). ETA next Wed. Will include token cost projections. :spiral_calendar:

Ravi (Sales): For the private deployment ask — customers want a checklist for network & KMS setup. Can we provide a checklist + estimated time to live?

Marta (Eng Manager): We can. Suggested content: network ports, VPC peering steps, KMS key rotation note, and sizing guidance per concurrency. I'll draft the checklist.

Elena (Customer Success): Also request from field: a simple migration matrix that says "When to pick hosted vs dedicated vs private" with 3 example customer profiles. That helped prospects in demos.

Ava (CEO): Good — prioritize materials that reduce friction in the buying process. Sam, please rank the deliverables by impact/effort and we'll staff accordingly.

Sam (Head of Product): My suggested priority (high -> low): 1) SLO templates + sample configs, 2) Private deployment checklist + TL;DR, 3) Quantization how-to, 4) Migration matrix.

Ravi (Sales): For the migration matrix, include a one-line objection rebuttal for each profile (e.g., "I can't risk unpredictable costs" -> "Use Dedicated with reserved capacity + token-level alerts").

Jordan (Growth): I'll create a short landing + CTAs for these resources so PLG users can self-serve. Suggest we also add a short in-console pointer (help bubble) for SLO templates.

Marta (Eng Manager): Technical follow-up: we should include a small benchmark table: throughput (tokens/s) for typical prompt sizes on our supported GPUs + quantization modes. That helps sales set expectations.

Elena (Customer Success): Field note: a few customers said they lost deals because our docs didn't state rollback SLAs for model switches. Can we add a clear rollback policy?

Sam (Head of Product): Noted. I'll add a rollback policy snippet to the SLO docs.

Ava (CEO): Good catch. Also we heard a recurring qualitative ask: better error messaging in the console when a model variant isn't compatible. OpsBot, can you capture an actionable ticket pattern for that?

OpsBot: Created ticket #TI-4821 -> "Console: surface compatibility reasons for model variant failures" assigned to eng-console.

Marta (Eng Manager): I'll own the compatibility error work with eng-console. ETA two sprints.

Ravi (Sales): Prospects also asked for "unit economics by scale" examples — i.e., per-100k tokens monthly cost scenarios. Jordan, can you add that to the landing?

Jordan (Growth): Yup — adding a small cost calc widget and 3 example bundles.

Ava (CEO): To avoid duplication: Sam, consolidate all deliverables into a single tracking doc and add owners + target dates. Share it in this thread when ready.

Sam (Head of Product): Will do. Draft link (internal): https://redwood.internal/docs/allhands/customer-signal-actions — I'll populate today.

Elena (Customer Success): Field owners: we'll follow up with the two lost deals and offer a short technical review/checklist to reduce friction if they re-engage. I'll drop notes into CRM.

Ravi (Sales): Please ping me before any public doc goes live so I can prep deal-specific comms.

Ava (CEO): One final ask from leadership Q&A: let's create a single "wins & losses" one-slide summary for the next board packet showing top 3 win themes and top 3 loss themes + mitigations. Sam, Jordan — can you coordinate?

Jordan (Growth): On it. I'll draft the slide and loop in design.

Marta (Eng Manager): Technical checklist snippet (for the how-to doc):
```
- Verify GPU family and quantization support
- Test 1k token sample for latency baseline
- Enable KV cache for conversational workloads
- Configure fallback model variant (same API signature)
```
Elena (Customer Success): Love it. Can we add a short FAQ: "What to do if latency spikes after switchover?" with steps 1-3. I'll draft.

Ava (CEO): Thanks — this is actionable. If no objections, I'll mark these owners and ask managers to support resourcing. Please all add any missing items into Sam's doc.

Sam (Head of Product): Added the initial table and owners to the doc. I'll post the link when it's updated.

Ravi (Sales): Thanks all — feels like a good plan.

Jordan (Growth): :raised_hands:

Marta (Eng Manager): :shipit:

Ava (CEO): Closing this thread — will review progress in next ops sync. If you add items to the doc, ping me.

OpsBot: Reminder scheduled: follow-up sync in two weeks for ticket review.
